start: ^It is 03:12. The phone on the desk lights up with a page from the monitoring service: the customer portal is timing out for some users. It is not down for everyone.
^You are the only person awake. The incident channel has three messages and no decisions.
^Open the incident channel and page the on-call engineer
^Check the status page and go back to sleep

c-0: ^You open the channel, state the impact in one sentence and page the engineer. The response is immediate: "I'm here. What do we know?"
c-1: ^You restart the portal. Some users reconnect. The logs from the failure disappear with the container.
c-2: ^You decide it is probably a blip. Twenty minutes later the page arrives again, and now the support lead is awake too.

triage: ^The support lead sends a screenshot: a booking form that never finishes. The monitoring graph shows normal CPU and plenty of free memory. The proxy is still serving other routes.
^You have three things you can do before the next change.
^Capture the proxy logs and the container state before changing anything
^Ask the support lead which customers are affected

c-0: ^You save the proxy log, the container state and the current network connections. It takes four minutes. The evidence is now yours.
c-1: ^The support lead names three customers on the same mobile network. That is a pattern, not a coincidence.
c-2: ^The last deployment rolls back. The timeout rate drops. The failed request is gone, and so is the evidence you would need to explain it.

contain: ^The portal is still live, and the next failure is a matter of time. You need to stop the bleed without destroying the trail.
^Put the proxy in maintenance mode and stop the bleed
^Keep it live and watch for the next failure

c-0: ^You switch the proxy to a clear maintenance page. Customers see an honest message instead of a dead form.
c-1: ^You keep the service live and watch the graph. It fails again, and this time the support lead sees it before you do.

b: ^The evidence tells a story. A single upstream connection is being reused after it has already been closed. The proxy retries it forever, and the booking form waits.
^You have a fix that makes the pain stop, but not a cause. The next failure will arrive with no explanation.

diagnose: ^Write the incident note with what you know and what you do not
^Close the incident because the service is up
^Escalate to the vendor and hand over the evidence
ending_root: ^You write the incident record: impact, timeline, evidence, cause and the one change that prevents a repeat. The support lead sends it to the customers before the morning shift.
^The next failure is less likely because the next person has a trail to follow.
ending_unknown: ^The service is stable and the customers are back. The incident record is thin: what you changed, not why it worked.
^You have bought time. The next failure will start from zero again.
ending_fragile: ^The portal is up, but the evidence is gone and the cause is still out there. Within a week the same timeout returns, and nobody can explain it.
^The lesson is not "restart faster". It is "capture first".
